podcast.body: This follow-up single was an "improbable smash in America" and a "seminal crossover track of early hip hop." On the song, Tom Tom Club combined "fluttery romantic lyrics with shout outs to black music history," name-checking artists like James Brown, Bootsy Collins, George Clinton, Bohannon, and Curtis Blow. It reached number 31 on the Hot 100 (higher than most Talking Heads singles) and a remarkable number two on the Soul Singles chart for a white rock act. It also became highly lucrative due to being sampled "dozens of times," including by Mariah Carey, Mark Morrison, and Lata. "Genius of Love was a seminal crossover track of early hip hop."
